assumptions: The region translated is in frame, as the `region` output states.
Biopython's translate semantics for ambiguity, stops and partial codons.
limits: Translates what it is given; it does not find the reading frame or the start codon.
bio.jane/contract.noReading: A transform: the protein a reading frame encodes under the genetic code given, with nothing inferred.
bio.jane/contract.question: What protein does this DNA encode, under the genetic code chosen?

description: Translate the subject DNA to protein (Biopython `Bio.Seq.translate` semantics). The SUBJECT is the selection when there is one, the named feature when `feature` is given, and the whole record otherwise — the `region` output says which, so never paste bases in to scope it.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

cds.description: strict CDS: require a length multiple of 3, a start codon and a terminal stop (errors otherwise). Advanced.

feature.description: translate this annotated coding feature by NAME instead of the selection (e.g. "ADH1"). A name the record does not annotate is refused with the names it does.

reverse.description: read the region as the reverse complement. Stated explicitly this always wins; left out, the selection's or the feature's own strand decides. Advanced.

to_stop.description: stop at the first stop codon instead of emitting the stop symbol.

name: translate_sequence

region.description: what was translated, and on which strand
